analysis.title: Supply Weakness Likely To Linger Into 2027: Refinery Outages Blow Past Goldman's Own Worst Case
key_insights: Goldman's Oil Products Tracker (Oct 25-26, 2026) says refined product supply stays tight into 2027 even as crude cools. Middle East refinery outages are about 1.6mb/d above seasonal norms and Russian outages 4.2mb/d above.
Deferred maintenance is expected to prolong product supply weakness into 2027. Planned maintenance rises sharply in 2027Q2 after an unusually light fall 2026 maintenance season.

Goldman's global average crude freight rate reached a new high of $24/bbl in October, versus about $3 a year ago. This squeezes net margins for refiners reliant on long-haul crude imports and pulls product tankers into crude hauling, reducing product shipping capacity.

Persian Gulf crude exports are at 92% of the 2025 level (15.3mb/d). Product exports lag: jet fuel at 54%, gasoil/diesel at 34% and gasoline at 10%. Ship-to-ship transfers that support crude flows are harder to replicate for products because of flammability and specification variability.

ZeroHedge's own arithmetic puts combined Middle East and Russian outages at roughly 5.8mb/d above seasonal norms. That exceeds the 5.0mb/d in Goldman's September 'Scenario 2' prolonged-disruption case (Bhandari). This sum is ZeroHedge's calculation, not Goldman's.

Planned global maintenance this fall is down 1.7mb/d (27%) y/y, largely from postponed US maintenance. Goldman says it comes due in 2027Q2, with the biggest rise relative to seasonal norms in Asia ex-China (India, South Korea).
Goldman warns high maintenance in India and South Korea could reduce product exports in 2027Q2, particularly diesel and jet fuel. Deferred maintenance also raises the risk of unplanned outages.

High-frequency product stocks remain low across major hubs. US gasoline and diesel stocks are below their historical range. China gasoline and diesel stocks are down 8% and 11% y/y, Singapore middle distillates are down 44%, and Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp jet fuel stocks are down 56% y/y.

Demand is weakening. Global average retail fuel prices are around $223/bbl, and Goldman nowcasts put European oil demand and US gasoline demand down 2% y/y. November jet demand is up only 73kb/d y/y, 3% below trend.

Goldman reiterates a recommendation to be long 2027 European summer gasoline as a hedge against geopolitical escalation. It first recommended the trade in mid-September in 'High Diesel Prices Cause High Gasoline Prices' and closed a European diesel spread for a potential 45% gain.
Goldman is bearish on crude despite being long products. It sees a war risk premium of nearly $25/bbl above fair value in Brent, expects $90 by December and an $80 average in 2027.

Crude is lower on Monday (Brent -1.4% to $115.04, WTI -2% to $101.24) on de-escalation efforts. Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish security officials are traveling to Iran. BofA's Francisco Blanch says $120 Brent is 'probably on the cards' if Iran resumes hitting regional infrastructure.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman expects refined product tightness to persist into 2027 on refinery outages, record freight, low inventories and a 2027Q2 maintenance wave, even as it expects crude's risk premium to fade.
Goldman sees Brent carrying a war risk premium near $25/bbl, forecasting $90 by December and an $80 average in 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Crude is lower on de-escalation headlines, but the note argues product markets are pricing physical supply constraints rather than headlines.
Same Monday de-escalation move as Brent.
Goldman expects the war risk premium to bleed out of crude while the products premium persists.
Record freight raises delivered costs and diverts product tankers to crude.
Gasoline shows the demand destruction; Goldman sees it as the cheap leg for a products long.
About 3.5x the gasoline crack (ZeroHedge's math); diesel remains very tight.
Strongest backwardation on record on a rolling basis, so the curve is not pricing a demand scare.
High retail prices weigh on demand, but have not eased supply tightness.
Per EIA via John Kemp. US refiners have no spare capacity left, and running flat out raises the odds of a long maintenance shutdown.

trade_ideas.rationale: Goldman says to hold it to hedge further geopolitical escalation against a highly uncertain Mideast and Russia supply outlook. Summer 2027 coincides with Asia's deferred maintenance peak.
trade_ideas.risk: A durable peace deal lets Russian and Gulf refineries get repaired before next spring and the hedge expires worthless (per ZeroHedge).

risk_factors: Durable peace deal that allows refinery repairs before spring 2027, which would hurt the long gasoline hedge.
Further Iranian attacks on regional infrastructure could push Brent to $120.
Deferred maintenance raises the risk of unplanned refinery outages.
Low product inventories at major hubs leave limited buffers against supply disruptions.
Continued Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries.
Demand destruction from $223/bbl retail fuel prices.
ZeroHedge notes OAT spreads and 5% Treasury yields already pressure central banks.
charts_described: Goldman chart (Kpler, Goldman Sachs GIR): latest Persian Gulf exports at 92% of the 2025 level for crude (15.3mb/d), 54% for jet fuel, 34% for gasoil/diesel and 10% for gasoline.

Goldman Exhibit 2 (IIR, Goldman Sachs GIR; seasonal norm is the 2018-2025 median excluding 2020): planned maintenance for 2027 peaks around 7.7mb/d near May versus about 6mb/d at this year's peak, and the Asia ex-China bar for Q2 2027 is well over 140% of its seasonal norm (readings by ZeroHedge).
vol_and_positioning: Brent Dec-Dec spread at $29.98/bbl is the strongest rolling backwardation on record.
Goldman's trading desk framed the war premium ending as 'sell the news, or $120' (from a Friday note referenced in the article).
geopolitical: US-Iran standoff continues. Top security officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are traveling to Iran to try to de-escalate.
Ukraine continues to strike Russian refineries despite Trump's proclaimed 'energy ceasefire'.
Washington is importing Russian diesel under a Trump-Moscow fuel deal.
Hormuz shipping requires war-risk premiums and security costs, including crew compensation for strike risk.
BofA's Blanch says $120 Brent is likely if Iran resumes hitting regional infrastructure.
The G7 emergency release of 100MM barrels came after Trump's diesel threat.
cross_bank_references: BofA's head of commodities Francisco Blanch told Bloomberg TV that $120 a barrel is 'probably on the cards' if Iran goes back to hitting regional infrastructure.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees products staying tight into 2027 on refinery outages above its own worst case, record freight, Gulf product exports at 10-54% of normal for gasoline to jet, low hub inventories and a 2027Q2 maintenance wave. BofA's Blanch says $120 Brent is likely if Iran resumes attacks.
tension_points.bear_case: Goldman expects the crude war premium of nearly $25/bbl to bleed out, with Brent at $90 by December and $80 in 2027. Retail fuel at $223/bbl is cutting demand, with gasoline demand down 2% y/y.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A durable peace deal that lets Russian and Gulf refineries be repaired before spring 2027 would leave the summer gasoline hedge worthless.

theme_stances.key_argument: Refinery outages, record freight, low Gulf product exports, thin inventories and deferred maintenance keep product supply tight into 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: Supply Weakness Likely to Linger into 2027
